qt: to the Commission Ciarán Cuffe (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The EU should be a manifestation of fairness and equality, including within its institutions. However, recent reports suggest that the institutions could do much more to reinforce opportunity and equality in their hiring processes. In the first instance, there is a distinct lack of minority groups reflected in the staffing of the EU institutions. In addition, there were reported complaints early last year regarding the EU’s transition to online recruitment, outlining the inequalities that can arise when altering the hiring process in this manner. Some candidates claimed that the process being solely online ‘violates equal opportunity, fueling inequality and driving talent away from the EU bubble1’. 1.
What measures are being taken to enhance accessibility for all applicants of our Member States when applying to jobs within the EU institutions, both online and in person?

What measures will the Commission take to encourage equal opportunities for all EU citizens, thereby ensuring diversity is reflected among the staff of the EU institutions, including but not limited to regarding gender, sexual orientation, disability, race or ethnic origin?
at: (English version) to the Commission Ciarán Cuffe (Verts/ALE) (23 February 2024) Subject: Reflecting diversity in the EU institutions The EU should be a manifestation of fairness and equality, including within its institutions. However, recent reports suggest that the institutions could do much more to reinforce opportunity and equality in their hiring processes. In the first instance, there is a distinct lack of minority groups reflected in the staffing of the EU institutions. In addition, there were reported complaints early last year regarding the EU’s transition to online recruitment, outlining the inequalities that can arise when altering the hiring process in this manner. Some candidates claimed that the process being solely online ‘violates equal opportunity, fueling inequality and driving talent away from the EU bubble (1)’. 1. What measures are being taken to enhance accessibility for all applicants of our Member States when applying to jobs within the EU institutions, both online and in person? 2. What measures will the Commission take to encourage equal opportunities for all EU citizens, thereby ensuring diversity is reflected among the staff of the EU institutions, including but not limited to regarding gender, sexual orientation, disability, race or ethnic origin? (12 June 2024) External competitions are managed by the European Personnel Selection Office (EPSO), which is an interinstitutional office. The Commission, together with other EU institutions, participates in its Management Board. EPSO’s selections are designed to be clear, transparent and accessible to all candidates. The goal is to provide all an equal opportunity by removing blocking factors, possible biases and risks of discrimination. EPSO’s selections will be run in the EU 24 languages, reflecting the linguistic diversity. Reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates may include physical accessibility, extended test time, magnification software, Braille materials, adapted lighting, and individual assistance. EPSO is renewing its partnerships on test platform delivery and is looking to further improve candidate experience. Online testing is the preferred choice given its convenience, modernity, greenness and cost-efficiency, as it is accessible to candidates wherever they are. The Commission is committed to building a more diverse and inclusive workplace. In 2021, it set up a Diversity and Inclusion Office to steer this work (2). Based on a staff survey and extensive internal consultations, an updated Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan 2023 — 2024 (3) was adopted, providing a clear framework for this work. In all recruitments, the Commission refers to the principle of equal opportunities and invites all qualified candidates to apply. Upon request, it provides candidates with targeted assistance throughout the recruitment process and raises awareness of recruitment panels on its equal opportunities policy. The Commission is committed to ensuring a geographically balanced workforce.
